trajectory_summary: This call opens already compromised — the customer was previously disqualified by Ion itself and is frustrated by repeat contact. The rep tries a tree-trimming workaround and a manager check rather than immediately validating the existing DQ, and the call ends with the customer restating the same conclusion the rep confirms four minutes later, plus an explicit removal-from-list request. Energy leaks steadily from guarded to resistant to an exit with a do-not-call ask.
outcome_dispute: Establishing the outcome here: this is a disqualification, not a fresh setter opportunity. The customer had already been told by Ion that shade/orientation ruled the home out, and the rep's own manager check at 02:44 confirms this. The call should be logged as a dq/no_appointment with an added do-not-call flag rather than treated as a standard missed-booking call.

observed_outcome.quote: So you were right. We're not allowed to do anything because it is too shaky.
observed_outcome.reasoning: The rep's manager-confirmed conclusion, combined with the customer's explicit request to be removed from the contact list, closes this as a hard disqualification rather than any form of booked, tentative, or callback outcome.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: No specific bill amount or usage figure was ever exchanged; the customer only speaks in relative terms ('half of the power bill') while arguing solar wouldn't help, and the call never reaches a bill-collection step due to the shade/DQ discussion dominating.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never reaches the standard 'what interested you in solar' question; the call is consumed entirely by the customer's re-assertion of a prior disqualification and the rep's attempt to find a workaround.

script_coverage.quote: Hey. It's Bucky with Ion. I'm reaching out about the solar form you still got online.
Oh, yeah. These do you have tall trees?
I was told that solar will not work on my house

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Recognize and close out hard DQs faster instead of improvising saves
primary_coaching_focus.quote: Well, I can here. I can help you get a phone call. That way you don't have to sit and meet with anybody and waste your time.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The customer disclosed a prior Ion-issued DQ and repeated contact complaints in the first 30 seconds; the rep spent nearly 4 minutes proposing workarounds (map check, tree trimming, a vague phone-call offer, manager escalation) before confirming what the customer already knew. Faster DQ recognition would protect the customer's time and the rep's, and would surface the do-not-call request sooner.

key_moments.quote: By your company, and you guys keep calling me and texting me.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer is flagging that this is a repeat/recycled contact on a lead Ion already disqualified. The rep proceeds with a standard qualify flow instead of recognizing this as a re-contact of a closed record.

key_moments.quote: I just I'm a little did they say why it wouldn't work? Because I'm looking on the map, so it looks fine.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep transparently admits uncertainty and pulls up a satellite/mapping tool live rather than dismissing the customer's claim outright. This is the 'admit and recover with transparency' pattern, which is the better of the three knowledge-gap responses the schema tracks.

key_moments.quote: I mean, I could try to see what we could do. Are you willing to, like, use trimming trees?
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep never captured a bill number or usage figure before proposing a technical workaround; the offer to trim trees is a specific fix pitched with no anchor to the customer's actual bill pain, so there's nothing pulling her back in emotionally even if trimming were feasible.

key_moments.quote: there's not enough surface area on the back of the house that doesn't get shade or gets enough sun to take away the power bill. It's not worth it.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is a technical roof/orientation/shading assessment the customer is delivering, and the correct setter move is to route it to a specialist for an actual site evaluation rather than adjudicate feasibility on a phone call. The rep instead continues to informally assess feasibility live (map look, trimming question) rather than deferring to design/specialist review.
